task.description: ELIXIR-DEV (WF-02 Step 2a) for REQ-156. Implement lib/letflow/design/req156-lua-memory-limit-impl.md, which passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR after 1 rework round (literal-code fix only, substance approved first pass). Read it in full before starting -- it already resolved the hardest technical question (Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 cannot carry a spawn_opt like max_heap_size, verified against real Elixir source) and specifies the exact alternative mechanism to implement. Extend lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex: add a :max_heap_words option (nil = unconstrained, matching REQ-149's exact shape) to execute_with_manifest/3. When nil, keep the existing REQ-155 Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 + Task.yield/2 + Task.shutdown path completely unchanged. When a positive integer is configured, branch to a separate execution path using :erlang.spawn_opt/2 with [:monitor, max_heap_size: %{size: max_heap_words, kill: true, error_logger: false}] instead of Task.Supervisor, with the caller's own bounded receive/timeout standing in for Task.yield/2, and Process.exit(pid, :kill) standing in for Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) if the caller's own timeout fires first. Resolve the :killed-reason ambiguity (a BEAM heap-kill and a caller-issued timeout-kill both produce :killed) exactly as the design specifies -- structurally, by message-arrival ordering (a :killed DOWN received before the caller's own kill was issued can only be the BEAM's own heap enforcement), not by inspecting the reason atom. Add the new {:error, :memory_limit_exceeded} result, pattern-distinguishable from REQ-154's {:error, {:budget_exceeded, _}} and REQ-155's {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, _}}. Add the moduledoc content the design requires (LUA-09 restated, terminate clause MET / fail-gracefully clause NOT MET per REQ-149's finding, :max_instructions rejected as a memory proxy per decision 0014 OQ-1). Write real functional tests per the design's test-suite section and test/specs/REQ-156.md -- critically, LUA-09's own acceptance criterion names a specific test scale ('a script attempting to allocate 1 GB with 16 MB limit fails cleanly') -- test at that scale or a proportionally realistic one, not a scale chosen purely for test convenience. Do not touch lib/letflow/engine/lua/capabilities.ex or platform.ex (unrelated, merged REQ-157 work). Follow the standard Step 2a procedure: verify branch, implement, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, self-review checklist. Given this run's own recent history (REQ-155 needed 2 rework rounds from insufficient test-run confidence), run scripts/test_parallel.sh at least twice before reporting PASS, not just mix test on the one file. No migrations needed.
acceptance_criteria: A test drives two different configured max_heap_words limits and asserts the smaller one halts an allocating script sooner

A test attempts a large allocation under a small configured limit at the scale LUA-09's own acceptance criterion names (not a convenience-scale substitute), asserting a structured error rather than a hang/node-exhaustion/success
The memory-limit error is pattern-distinguishable from REQ-154's and REQ-155's error shapes, asserted by a test matching each of the three arms specifically
No code path uses :max_instructions as a memory-limit proxy
Moduledoc states which LUA-09 clause is met (terminate) and which is not (fail gracefully), in those words
At least 2 scripts/test_parallel.sh full-suite runs quoted, not just one file's tests

result.notes:
Implemented REQ-156 per lib/letflow/design/req156-lua-memory-limit-impl.md, faithfully: added :max_heap_words (nil | pos_integer()) to execute_with_manifest/2,3. nil keeps the REQ-155 Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 + Task.yield/2 + Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) path byte-for-byte unchanged (verified: all 12 pre-existing REQ-154/155 call sites in executor_test.exs pass unmodified once max_heap_words: nil was added to their opts). A positive integer branches to new private run_with_heap_limit/4, which bypasses Task.Supervisor entirely (per design §2's Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2,3 finding) and spawns via :erlang.spawn_opt/2 with [:monitor, max_heap_size: %{size: max_heap_words, kill: true, error_logger: false}]. Uses two distinct refs: a caller-generated reply_ref (tags the {ref, reply} completion message, since the child cannot know the BIF's atomically-returned monitor_ref in advance) and the spawn_opt :monitor ref (tags :DOWN messages). The caller's own bounded receive/after stands in for Task.yield/2; Process.exit(pid, :kill) stands in for Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) on the caller's own timeout. The :killed ambiguity is resolved structurally, not by reason atom: a :killed DOWN arriving in the primary receive clause (before the `after timeout_ms` branch has fired) can only be the BEAM's own max_heap_size kill, since the caller only issues its own kill inside the `after` branch, after nothing was observed within timeout_ms -- see executor.ex's run_with_heap_limit/4 comments and its mirrored moduledoc REQ-156 section. Added {:error, :memory_limit_exceeded} as a new arm on both @spec unions (bare atom, structurally distinct from {:budget_exceeded, _} and {:wallclock_timeout, _}). Added default_max_heap_words/0 (Application.fetch_env!(:letflow, :lua_max_heap_words)) mirroring default_budget/0 and default_timeout_ms/0; added config :letflow, lua_max_heap_words: nil to config/config.exs (production default: unconstrained, per design §10 OQ-1 -- ELIXIR-DEV's choice, no operational data yet to justify a tuned value). Did not touch capabilities.ex or platform.ex. No migrations. Moduledoc gained a full REQ-156 section: LUA-09 restated with 'terminate the script' is MET / 'fail gracefully' is NOT MET (both stated in those exact words), the Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2,3 cannot-carry-max_heap_size finding stated plainly, the :max_instructions-rejected-as-memory-proxy statement citing decision 0014 OQ-1 by name, the branching mechanism, and the observability divergence (memory-limited executions are not Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor children).

Test suite: added a new 'configurable memory limit (REQ-156)' describe block to test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs (11 new tests) covering AC-1 through AC-6, plus a regression test proving the nil-limit path still runs under Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor exactly as REQ-155 established. AC-2's test uses the literal 1 GB attempted / 16 MB limit scale LUA-09's own acceptance criterion names, unscaled, converted via :erlang.system_info(:wordsize) rather than a hardcoded byte-to-word literal. AC-1's two-different-limits comparison uses a smaller allocating script (~20 MB attempted vs a ~1 MB limit, a ~1:20 ratio, same order of magnitude as AC-2's ~1:64 ratio) purely for test speed -- running the full 1 GB script to unkilled completion (needed for AC-1's 'larger limit succeeds' arm) was measured at ~18s real time in this environment (tv-labs/lua interpreter throughput, not the mechanism under test), which is documented in a code comment as the reason for scaling down that one arm; AC-2's own dedicated test keeps the full, unscaled 1 GB/16 MB scale.
